acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: When Danielle's family serves poultry at their dinner table, no one utters the word "chicken." Instead, it is always called "fish." Danielle explains why with the help of her friend "Duki."
acts.title: Duki

acts.label: Act Five Preview
acts.desc: Chickenman was a short daily radio show airing from 1966 to 1969, and it was incredibly popular. It started locally on WCFL in Chicago, then proceeded to spread to over 1,500 radio stations. It has been translated into German, into Dutch, into Swedish. It is still on the air even today in several dozen markets, making it one of the longest running radio features anywhere.
acts.title: Chickenman

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Julie Showalter, who grew up on a turkey farm, tells the story of the night 3,000 turkeys died.
acts.title: Turkey

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Writer David Sedaris tells of the giddiness he felt when he purchased a taxidermy's turkey head— attached to its foot. (2 1/2 minutes)

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Michael Stumm on the uses of chickens in South African sangoma (witch doctor) culture.
acts.title: South African Chicken Blood

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: We invited Dick Orkin to create a new Chickenman episode for our Poultry Slam. He put a cast together and created the first new episode since 1969.
acts.title: Chickenman, Like The Phoenix
